title: CONDA Condensed Deep Association Learning for Co-Salient Object Detection

predicted_errors.error_location: Introduction, paragraph describing PAG ("PAG progressively generates association features on varying scales...")
predicted_errors.supporting_evidence: The text claims that progressive enhancement in PAG improves 'the association quality from the very beginning.' However, Eq. (3) explicitly states the iteration runs 's ranges from 5 to 3' with the initialization '{F̂_{5,l}} = {F_{5,l}}', meaning the coarsest/first-processed stage (s=5) uses the raw, unenhanced VGG backbone features with no prior association feature to enhance it. This is exactly the 'raw-association-based' limitation the paper criticizes in prior work. Thus the claim that quality is improved 'from the very beginning' contradicts the method's own initialization, since the first hyperassociation computed (at stage 5) receives no enhancement at all.

predicted_errors.error_location: Section on Correspondence-induced Association Condensation (CAC), two figure references
predicted_errors.supporting_evidence: The text first states that the condensation of pixel associations between a single pixel and a single target image 'A_s(i,h_i,w_i,j,:,:,:)... as shown in Figure 3,' and then later states that the generalized condensation across all images, 'a_s ∈ R^{N×Hs×Ws×Ls}, in Figure 2.' Figure 2 was already defined earlier as the overall CONDA architecture diagram ('As shown in Figure 2, CONDA integrates the deep association learning process into an FPN framework'), not as an illustration of pixel-to-all-images condensation. Referencing the more general case with an earlier-numbered figure than the simpler single-pixel case (Figure 3) is inconsistent with normal figure ordering and conflicts with the stated content of Figure 2.

predicted_errors.error_location: Ablation study, 'Effectiveness of CAC' paragraph and MACs reduction claim
predicted_errors.supporting_evidence: The paper states CAC condenses the full hyperassociation's target spatial dimension from H_s×W_s pixels down to a fixed K×K=81 window (K=9), which for typical feature map sizes (e.g., 32×32 or 64×64) represents a reduction of well over 90% in the number of target-pixel associations per source pixel. Yet the reported computational savings for the aggregation network are only from 91.38G to 77.19G MACs (~15.5% reduction). This large discrepancy between the claimed drastic reduction in hyperassociation size and the comparatively small reported compute savings is not explained and is inconsistent with the stated motivation that CAC 'reduces the multiply-accumulate operations... and enhances the quality of deep association features' through massive pixel condensation.
